feedback: Approve. This candidate matches iteration 1, the best raced build (62.18), field for field: ki 0.4, kp 2.5, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4, line_loss last_direction, sensor weights [2, 1, 0, -1, -2], outer sensors at x = ±0.03 m and inner at ±0.015 m. The rationale and geometry agree. Across iterations 0 to 4, every run went off track, with exactly one line-loss event per run, max_error at the 0.06 m limit, and progress between 0.10 and 0.17. Iteration 2 (ki 1.0) scored 59.93 and iteration 3 (sensors widened to ±0.045 m) scored 56.65, so neither change beat the baseline. Nothing here predicts how this candidate will perform. Only one run remains and no review-and-revise round fits, so a revise decision would leave the iteration unscored. Approval is the only option that gets a score. Consider this a repeat of the best evidence. The measurements from this race are the last data for the record.
requested_changes: Record for the next team: if the race again shows one line-loss event per run with progress near 0.17, the next change to test is line_loss = search_right in place of last_direction, because iteration 1 never tested the search direction.

Record for the next team: if any run finishes with completion_time at or above about 2.8 s, the next change is base_speed from 1.4 to about 1.5 to 1.6, since 1.4 is slower than the roughly 1.5 m/s the contract needs for a sub-3 s finish.

Record for the next team: if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 while max_error stays under 0.06, lower kp from 2.5 toward 2.2 before changing kd, because the gain increase since iteration 0 is the likeliest source of extra jitter.
